summary:
[  edit  ]
The MIDI In  CHOP  reads Note events, Controller events, Program Change events, System Exclusive messages and Timing events from both MIDI devices and files. See also  MIDI In Map CHOP .
The MIDI In  CHOP  receives  MIDI  events from MIDI devices connected to the serial port, reads MIDI events internal to the workstation (i.e. the built-in software synth), and interprets musical scores in MIDI files. Supported MIDI events are:
Note On, Note Off
Polyphonic Aftertouch
Channel Pressure
Program Change
Control Change (MIDI controller devices)
Pitch Wheel
Timer Events including beat pulses
Bar Messages
Start, Stop, Continue
Song Position Pointer
System Exclusive Messages   MIDI events arriving on separate MIDI channels may be recorded on separate  CHOP  channels. Also, any number of MIDI CHOPs can read from the same or different sources. TouchDesigner can be configured such that MIDI Start, Stop, or Continue events can control the  Timeline  and  Beat Dialog .
The 'Simplified Output' option creates a channel for every type of MIDI event received, so number of channels expands while the devices is being used. No need to specify name, channel and index patterns.
Note : The values of the MIDI inputs are saved into the TouchDesigner  .toe  file, and are restored when the file is reloaded. The physical controllers may be in a different position when the  .toe  is restarted, causing the values to jump when the controllers are moved. This is unavoidable.
See also the  MIDI In DAT ,  MIDI Event DAT ,  MIDI In Map CHOP ,  MIDI Out CHOP .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Enable or disable the MIDI In  CHOP .

parameters.label: MIDI Source
parameters.name: source
parameters.description: ⊞  - Get MIDI input from a device or a file.

parameters.label: Device
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: The MIDI events come live from a device.

parameters.label: File
parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The MIDI events come from an existing file.

parameters.label: Device Table
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Path  to the MIDI device  Table DAT

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Specify the id of which device to use.

parameters.label: MIDI File
parameters.name: file
parameters.description: If MIDI file is selected as the MIDI source use this field to specify the name of the MIDI file to read. The file can be read in from disk or from the web. Use http:// when specifying a URL.

parameters.label: Read Entire MIDI File
parameters.name: entire
parameters.description: If enabled, the entire MIDI file is read. Otherwise, the Start and End parameters on the Channel page determine the segment of the file to read.

parameters.label: Reset	Channels
parameters.name: resetchannels
parameters.description: Deletes all channels when set to On, new channels will not be added until Reset Channels is turned Off.

parameters.label: Reset Channels  Pulse
parameters.name: resetchannelspulse
parameters.description: Instantly deletes all channels.

parameters.label: Reset	Values
parameters.name: resetvalues
parameters.description: Resets all channel values to 0 when On, channel values will not be updated until Reset Values is turned Off.

parameters.label: Reset Channels  Pulse
parameters.name: resetchannelspulse
parameters.description: Instantly resets all channels to 0.

parameters.label: Simplified Output
parameters.name: simplified
parameters.description: When this is on channels are automatically created when MIDI signal is detected from the selected MIDI device.

parameters.label: Preserve Pulses
parameters.name: preservepulses
parameters.description: When on, quick value transitions (pulses) are spaced out over consecutive output samples. Use this option when pulse frequencies approach or exceed the timeline rate, otherwise they risk overlapping each other and being lost.

parameters.label: 1 Based Index
parameters.name: onebased
parameters.description: Make the index 1 based instead of the default 0 based, which means that the indices will belong to the range 1-128 instead of 0-127. The value of this parameter affects the Note and Controller indices.

parameters.label: MIDI Channels
parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The  CHOP  may read from any number of MIDI channels, numbered 1-16. Ranges and multiple entries are supported (i.e. "1 4 6", "1-7 12", "1-5:2").

parameters.label: Channel Prefix
parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: When recording from multiple MIDI channels, putting a string like "ch" in this parameter causes the MIDI channel to be split into separate  CHOP  channels per MIDI channel. Otherwise the MIDI channels are all merged into one set of  CHOP  channels.

parameters.label: Controller Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Some controllers can be paired together to form 14 bit controllers, rather than the normal 7 bit controllers (controller indices 0-31, 98 and 100). Selecting 14 bit Controllers interprets a pair as one 14 bit controller. Otherwise, they are interpreted as separate 7 bit Controllers.

parameters.label: 7 bit Controllers
parameters.name: 7bit
parameters.description: Controllers are assumed to be regular 7 bit value messages.

parameters.label: 14 bit Controllers
parameters.name: 14bit
parameters.description: Controllers are received as two 7 bit value messages.

parameters.label: Of the two messages, one is the MSB (Most Significant Byte) and the other is the LSB (Least Significant Byte), the values of which are combined to interpret the 14
parameters.description: bit value.

parameters.label: MSB message must be in the controller range 0
LSB message must be in the controller range 32
parameters.description: 63. And it's index should be MSB index + 32. i.e. if the MSB message has index 12, then the LSB message must have index 44.

parameters.label: If a single message in the range 0
parameters.description: 63 is received, then nothing will be outputted.

parameters.label: In this mode, messages in the index range 64
parameters.description: 95 will be interpreted as 7 bit and be outputted as such since the range 64-95 is reserved for 7 bit messages.

parameters.label: Record Method
parameters.name: recordtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine what to record.

parameters.label: Single  Frame
parameters.name: single
parameters.description: This only outputs the current value of notes, controllers, etc. It does not retain prior values. It creates a  CHOP  at frame 1 always, so the  CHOP  causes cooking only when MIDI events come in.

parameters.label: Current  Frame
parameters.name: current
parameters.description: Same as "Single  Frame ", but the  CHOP  frame is always at the current frame, so the  CHOP  changes every frame, causing other CHOPs to recook every frame.

parameters.label: Current  Time Slice
parameters.name: ind
parameters.description: The  CHOP  frame is always at the current  Time Slice .

parameters.label: Full Length
parameters.name: timeline
parameters.description: The entire length of the timeline is recorded.

parameters.label: Record
parameters.name: record
parameters.description: This parameter is used as a button to start and stop recording into the  CHOP  channels.

parameters.label: Note Name
parameters.name: notename
parameters.description: Put an "n" in here to generate channels for note events. It is the base name of the  CHOP  channel used to record notes. If blank, notes are ignored. If the Note Output parameter is set to Separate Channels, then  CHOP  channels will be created for each note in the Note  Scope , of the form: notename

parameters.label: Note  Scope
parameters.name: notescope
parameters.description: The scope of notes to record. Multiple ranges and notes can be recorded (i.e., "50-60", "64 65 66 70-80").

parameters.label: Note Output
parameters.name: notemeth
parameters.description: ⊞  - Describes how multiple notes are handled. (As one channel, or individual).

parameters.label: One Multiplexed  Channel
parameters.name: mult
parameters.description: One  CHOP  channel per MIDI channel is used for all notes. The value in the note channel is the number of the note currently playing (in the case of multiple notes playing, the most recent note is selected).

parameters.label: Separate Channels
parameters.name: sep
parameters.description: Each note number gets its own  CHOP  channel.

parameters.label: Velocity
parameters.name: velocity
parameters.description: ⊞  - Describes how multiple velocity events are recorded. (Separate channels or combined in one channel as separate samples).

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: veloff
parameters.description: Velocity is not recorded.

parameters.label: Note Amplitude
parameters.name: velencode
parameters.description: The velocity is recorded as the amplitude of the note. Only valid when Note Output is set to Separate Channels.

parameters.label: Separate Channels
parameters.name: velsep
parameters.description: Velocity is recorded in separate  CHOP  channels. Each note channel will have a corresponding velocity channel.

parameters.label: Velocity Name
parameters.name: velname
parameters.description: When Velocity is set to Separate Channels, this parameter is the base name of the Velocity  CHOP  channel (try "v"). If blank, no velocity channels will be recorded.

parameters.label: Aftertouch Name
parameters.name: aftername
parameters.description: The base name of the polyphonic Aftertouch  CHOP  channels. One aftertouch channel is created for each note in the Note  Scope . If blank, no aftertouch channels will be created.

parameters.label: Pressure Name
parameters.name: pressname
parameters.description: The name of the Channel Pressure channel. If multiple channels are being recorded, all channel pressure changes of interest will be recording on this  CHOP  channel. If blank, this channel will not be created.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: notenorm
parameters.description: ⊞  - Note values can be normalized for convenience:

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: When Normalize is Off, 7 bit controllers will return values in the range 0-127 and 14 bit controllers will return values in the range 0-16383.

parameters.label: 0 to 1
parameters.name: 0to1
parameters.description: These values are normalized to lie in the range 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Pitch Wheel Name
parameters.name: pitchname
parameters.description: The name of the Pitch Wheel  CHOP  channel. Pitch wheel values range from -1 to +1. If blank, this channel will not be created. Put "p" in here to generate a channel.

parameters.label: Controller Name
parameters.name: controlname
parameters.description: The base name of the Control Change  CHOP  channels. The channel names are appended with the controller index (0-127). If blank, control changes will not be recorded. It typically contains "c".

parameters.label: Controller Type
parameters.name: controltype
parameters.description: ⊞  - There are 128 different controllers available. By choosing By Index Only, you can specify any number of controllers in the Control Index parameter. Otherwise, you can select a controller from the list from this menu. Some controllers have multiple instances, such as Sound Controllers 1-10. Selecting a controller with multiple instances allows you to use the Control Index parameter to select which instances you want. Any invalid control indices will be ignored.

parameters.label: By Index Only
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Specify the controller by its index, as opposed to specifying a specific type below.

parameters.label: Non
parameters.description: Registered  Parameter    n22  -

parameters.label: Controller Index
parameters.name: controlind
parameters.description: Used to select controllers by number, or multiple controllers by ranges. When in By Index Only Controller Type mode, you can select up to the full 128 controllers or sub-ranges thereof (i.e. "1-10", "2 34 70", "1-32 70-80:2").

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: norm
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controller values can be normalized for convenience:

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: When Normalize is Off, 7 bit controllers will return values in the range 0-127 and 14 bit controllers will return values in the range 0-16383.

parameters.label: 0 to 1
parameters.name: 0to1
parameters.description: These values are normalized to lie in the range 0 to 1.

parameters.label: -1 to 1
parameters.description: 1to1  - These values are normalized to lie in the range -1 to +1.

parameters.label: On/Off
parameters.name: onoff
parameters.description: Several of the controllers are simply on/off states. When Convert to On/Off is enabled, values greater than or equal to 64 will be interpreted as "1" and all values less than 64 will be interpreted as "0".

parameters.label: Unwrap
parameters.name: unwrap
parameters.description: When on, values do not jump between min and max, but are modified to be continuous ramps. Use with knob controllers for examples.

parameters.label: Program Change
parameters.name: progname
parameters.description: The name of the Program Change  CHOP  channel. All program change messages will be recorded onto this channel. If blank, this channel will not be created.

parameters.label: Timer  Pulse  Name
parameters.name: pulsename
parameters.description: Record timer pulse messages.

parameters.label: Timer Ramp Name
parameters.name: rampname
parameters.description: Record timer ramp messages.

parameters.label: Timer Period
parameters.name: timerperiod
parameters.description: Record timer period messages.

parameters.label: Timer Start
parameters.name: timerstart
parameters.description: Record timer start messages.

parameters.label: Ticks per Beat
parameters.name: ticks
parameters.description: Specify the expected ticks per beat. This will influence the timer and bar output values.

parameters.label: Bar Ramp Name
parameters.name: barname
parameters.description: Output the current bar position.

parameters.label: Bar Period
parameters.name: barperiod
parameters.description: Output the current bar period events.

parameters.label: Bar Start
parameters.name: barstart
parameters.description: Output when a bar starts.

parameters.label: Bar Message
parameters.name: barmsg
parameters.description: Capture bar messages. Place a V in the message to specify which value the channel should have.

parameters.label: Song Pos Name
parameters.name: songpos
parameters.description: Capture song position messages.

parameters.label: System Exclusive
parameters.name: sysex
parameters.description: Sequence of system exclusive message handlers

parameters.label: Channel Name
parameters.name: sysex0name
parameters.description: Name of a specific exclusive message to be captured.

parameters.label: Message
parameters.name: sysex0msg
parameters.description: Contents of the exclusive message. Place a V in the message to specify which value the channel should have.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Defines where recording begins. In "Tie to Time Line" mode, any events received before the start time will be ignored. In "Time Line Independent" mode, recording will start at this point and continue on (not looping back). If reading from a MIDI File, Start/End will determine the start of the segment to read.

parameters.name: startunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units to use for this parameter, Samples, Frames, or Seconds.

parameters.label: I
parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Use samples.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: frames
parameters.description: Use frames.

parameters.label: S

parameters.label: End
parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Defines the end of the segment to read for MIDI Files.

parameters.label: End Unit
parameters.name: endunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units to use for this parameter, Samples, Frames, or Seconds.

parameters.label: I
parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Use samples.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: frames
parameters.description: Use frames.

parameters.label: S
parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: Use seconds.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: Defines the sample rate of this  CHOP , in samples per second. If the sample rate is too low, a rapidly changing input may be misrepresented.

parameters.label: Note : If the sample rate is too low, you may miss MIDI events. A note event may set a sample value to 1, and then the next note event less than 1/30 second later can set it to 0 on the same sample in the  CHOP  channel. So the event will be missed. Make the sample rate higher, like 600, to catch these events, or make sure that your on
parameters.description: off events coming in are a minimum time separation, as can be achieved through Opcode's MAX.

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: left
parameters.description: ⊞  - The left extend conditions (before range).

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Hold the current value of the channel.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Continue the slope before the start of the channel.

parameters.label: Cycle

parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Hold the current value of the channel.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Continue the slope after the end of the channel.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly, mirroring every other cycle.

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Use the constant value specified in the Default Value parameter.

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.name: defval
parameters.description: The value used for the Default Value extend condition.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter

parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root

parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length

parameters.label: sample_rate

parameters.label: num_channels

parameters.label: time_slice

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.
